title: Secure a cable in a terminal box's cord clamp
instruction: Secure the cable in the terminal box's cord clamp: slide the cable in until its sheath reaches at least 5 mm past the clamp bar and hold it there while you tighten the bar's two screws in turns with the hex screwdriver, so that the bar presses on the sheath and stays parallel. Then let go of the cable and the screwdriver.
context: Every machine or appliance with a fixed cable anchors it inside with a cord clamp, so that a pull on the cable doesn't reach the terminals; clamping the bare cores instead of the sheath, or a crooked or crushed clamp, is a classic inspection fault.
setup: All positions from the arm bases' midline (x forward, y left). Fixed on the table: a grey cast-aluminium terminal box, 150 mm deep x 155 mm wide x 60 mm tall, 4 mm walls, lid off, footprint centred at x 0.26 m, y 0.0025 m; a 12 x 12 mm cable entry in the middle of its right wall (centre 18 mm up); a blue terminal block (40 x 14 x 22 mm) at its left wall. Cord clamp 57 mm inside the entry wall: an aluminium saddle (36 x 10 mm, top 14 mm up), a steel clamp bar (32 x 8 x 3 mm, ribbed underside) resting across the cable, and two black M4 x 16 socket cap screws (3 mm hex socket, heads 7 mm across), 22 mm apart, started in the saddle, heads 1 mm above the bar; clockwise from above tightens, about 1.5 turns to contact. Cable: 3 x 1.5 mm2 control cable, grey PVC sheath 8 mm across; its cores (brown, blue, green-yellow, taped together) run 80 mm from the terminal block in a slight bow to the sheath's cut end, 1 mm short of the bar's centre line; the sheath runs level out through the entry, drops to the table 40 mm outside and lies there ~180 mm, curving 55 degrees toward the arms, far end free. The cores' bow is springy: pushed in and let go before the clamp grips it, the cable springs back until the sheath's cut end is about 3-5 mm past the bar's centre line (short of the 9 mm needed). A 3 mm hex screwdriver (80 mm, red handle 24 mm across) stands blade-down in a 40 x 40 x 30 mm steel holder at x 0.17 m, y 0.19 m.
scoring: Sheath past = the sheath's cut end at least 5 mm past the bar's edge toward the terminals (measured before a failed pull test). First contact = a screw head presses the bar (2 N, 0.5 s; finger-tight in a real trial); turns since are read on a mark. Snug = 0.25 to under 1.75 turns past first contact. In turns = the two screws' turns past first contact differ by less than 0.25 turn. Parallel = bar tilt under 2 degrees: the two screw heads' heights differ by less than 0.77 mm (22 mm apart). Pull test = once no fingertip or screwdriver tip has been within 60 mm of the heads, bar or cable near the clamp for 1 s and a head presses: 30 N outward on the cable outside the box (ramped 1 s, held 0.5 s); holds if the cable moves under 1 mm at the clamp. Score: 1.0 (success, ends the run) = sheath past, holds, both screws snug and in turns, bar parallel, hands off and parts still 1 s; 0.75 = same but not in turns or bar tilted 2 degrees or more; 0.5 = sheath past and holds, a screw not snug; 0.25 = sheath past only; 0 = otherwise, or (latched) the cores clamped: a head ever pressed 3 N for 0.25 s while the sheath's end wasn't past the bar, or the cable crushed: a screw ever 2 turns past first contact.
reset_notes: Unscrew both clamp screws to their start (heads 1 mm above the bar, about 1.5 turns before contact), pull the cable back until the sheath's cut end is 1 mm short of the bar's centre line, and lay it as in the screenshot; screwdriver back in its holder. A crushed cable must be replaced.
fidelity: CPU PhysX 240 Hz. Own simplified parts, no third-party CAD. Screws on jointed threads (0.7 mm/turn) with joint friction and a 60 N/mm spring under each head (the bar's and sheath's give); the bar presses the cable by contact (friction 0.8). Cable: 20 mm links with bending/torsion springs, rooted at the terminals; the sheath takes a creeping set, the cores' bow stays elastic (it pushes the cable back). Crushed = turns past contact (no damage model). Bar at 60 g. Pull test applied by the task.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; scripted demo: 1.0 (success at step 6,595); cable held, screws tightened alternately but unevenly: 0.75; one screw barely touching: 0.25; pushed in, let go, then tightened: 0.0; pushed in and let go: 0.0; tightened on the cores: 0.0
